images.filename: Bristol Temple Meads Station and an Up LMR express 2093479 27e4170c.jpg
images.caption:
Bristol Temple Meads Station and an Up LMR express.
Via westward, from the north/east end of No. 9 platform. The 08.50 Paignton to Leeds express stands at No. 7 platform with LMS Fowler Class 6P 4-6-0 No. 45506 'The Royal Pioneer Corps', which has just taken over for the journey up the ex-Midland main line via Birmingham (New St.). In the centre road is an ex-LMS 4F 0-6-0 No. 44560.
images.alt:
Bristol Temple Meads Station and an Up LMR express.
Via westward, from the north/east end of No. 9 platform. images.filename: Bristol Temple Meads Station, original terminus with steam train and Diesel railcar - geograph.org.uk - 2124234.jpg
images.caption:
Bristol Temple Meads Station, original terminus with steam train and Diesel railcar, near to Bristol, Great Britain.
View westward, towards the uffer-stops in the original Brunel terminus at Temple Meads. On the left at Platform 13 is LMS Compound 4P 4-4-0 No. 41062 on the 10.52 stopping train for Gloucester; on the right at Platform 15 is a Diesel railcar set on the service to Severn Beach.
images.alt:
Bristol Temple Meads Station, original terminus with steam train and Diesel railcar, near to Bristol, Great Britain.
View westward, towards the uffer-stops in the original Brunel terminus at Temple Meads. On the left at Platform 13 is LMS Compound 4P 4-4-0 No. 41062 on the 10.52 stopping train for Gloucester; on the right at Platform 15 is a Diesel railcar set on the service to Severn Beach.

images.caption:
Bristol Parkway railway station, GloucestershireOpened in 1972 by British Rail where its lines from Birmingham to Bristol and London to South Wales cross.
View west towards Bristol and South Wales from the east-bound platform. When opened there were only 2 platform faces, a modest car park and a small booking hall. By 2021 the car park was double decked (far right), a larger booking hall had been opened (centre right), there were 4 platform faces and the railway line had been electrified.
images.alt:
Bristol Parkway railway station, GloucestershireOpened in 1972 by British Rail where its lines from Birmingham to Bristol and London to South Wales cross.
View west towards Bristol and South Wales from the east-bound platform. When opened there were only 2 platform faces, a modest car park and a small booking hall. By 2021 the car park was double decked (far right), a larger booking hall had been opened (centre right), there were 4 platform faces and the railway line had been electrified.
